summary.headline: Hero Motors Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 318 crore, with PAT up 49% to INR 24 crore and PAT margin at 7.3%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 27% YoY to INR 318 crore and EBITDA rose 35% to INR 47 crore, with EBITDA margin at 40.4% as stated on the call. Consolidated revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 365 crore, with consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.8% for the quarter per the call. For H1 FY27, consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR 684 crore and PAT rose 84% to INR 28 crore. Management said the power train business now contributes about 52% of revenue and debt-to-equity fell from 0.89x to 0.21x. Management guided to 20%+ revenue growth for the full year and continued investment in new facilities such as Bangalore and STP.

financial_highlights.change: +62% YoY from INR 11 crore; margin +125 bps

financial_highlights.value: INR 684 crore; EBITDA INR 87 crore, margin 12.5%

segments.name: Alloy & Metallic (ANM)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 174 crore (+24% YoY), 48% of revenue; H1 FY27 INR 330 crore (+26%). Management cites new domestic and European customers and products; margin about 6-7%.

segments.name: Gears & Transmission (GNT)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 142 crore (+16% YoY), 39% of revenue; H1 FY27 INR 265 crore (+15%). Management cites a 5-year revenue CAGR above 30% and segment margin of 23-25%.

segments.name: Bike Power Train (EV/hybrid)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 48 crore (+27% YoY), 13% of revenue; H1 FY27 INR 89 crore (+37%). Management said FY26 grew about 50%; steady-state margin is expected to be similar to GNT, with EDU revenue INR 27 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%+ YoY; management expects consolidated EBITDA margin to rise versus last year.
Standalone margin expected around 14% in the full year per management.
New Bangalore EDU facility to start around March-April 2027; INR 60-80 crore revenue in FY28 and about INR 200 crore (+/-10%) in FY29 from confirmed orders.
Interest cost to fall to INR 1.5-2 crore per quarter after repaying INR 190 crore of loans (originally about INR 410 crore).

Capex of about INR 200 crore from IPO proceeds over the next two years, plus about INR 150 crore of maintenance capex; INR 350 crore total growth capex expected including the STP facility (about 50% of it for the STP facility).
Over the medium term, management expects system-level margin uplift of about 100 bps, with GNT steady state at 24-25%.
capex_capacity: GNT operates at about 70-75% capacity utilisation; Bike Power Train at about 70-75% in one facility; ANM at about 70-75%, expected to be slightly lower until STP ramps up.
Bangalore EDU facility: orders already confirmed; customer River to be a 100% supplier for transmission systems for electric bikes and scooters; ramp-up over about one year.

STP (Germany JV) forging and machining facility: manufacturing expected to start in calendar 2027 with about 70% of revenue from global markets; investment about USD 10 million over 3-5 years for high-precision forging.
Hero Thailand facility serves BMW Thailand, with plans to also supply BMW Germany from it; a new project is expected to start from January 2027.
demand_pricing: Order book: about INR 4,000 crore lifetime revenue on confirmed projects of 5-8 years (sometimes up to 12), equating to about INR 500-600 crore of annual revenue at full ramp; about INR 100-150 crore starts within FY27, with full ramp by FY28-29.
Formula racing transmission supply starts by end of calendar 2026.
Marine: design fees of INR 5-20 crore per project; serial production could be significantly larger.
Power train: about 70-75% of revenue from global markets; total company overseas revenue about 37-40%.
System margins 18-25% versus ANM at about 6-8%; management said components are lower margin and capital intensive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the confirmed order book within the INR 4,000 crore pipeline, and when does the annual ramp-up reach INR 500-600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the projects are confirmed by customers, with 5-8 year life cycles; about INR 100-150 crore starts in FY27 and the full INR 500-600 crore annual run-rate is expected by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: How significant is the marine application, and what is the order size?
qa_highlights.answer: This is the second or third marine order; the current order is a design fee of about INR 5-6 crore, with a range of INR 5-20 crore per design project and potentially large serial production later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potential and customers for the new Bangalore facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR 60-80 crore revenue in FY28 and about INR 200 crore (+/-10%) in FY29; River will be a 100% supplier, with Ather also to be served.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook and the interest-cost trajectory after debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it invests INR 125-150 crore a year in growth; INR 200 crore from IPO proceeds over two years, plus about INR 150 crore maintenance capex. INR 190 crore of loans were repaid, and quarterly interest cost is expected at INR 1.5-2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the STP facility timeline, order book and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing expected to start in calendar 2027, with about 70% of revenue from global markets; asset turnover expected around 1.5x; order book not yet shared.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margins outpace consolidated margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone reflects established businesses, while subsidiaries (EDU, Hero Thailand and others) are in growth phase; some expect break-even in FY27 and others in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth and margin outlook, and how is raw material cost pass-through handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 20%+ revenue growth and a higher EBITDA margin than last year; the pass-through mechanism was not detailed on the call.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT margin of 4.9% in Q2 is well below the standalone 7.3%, as subsidiaries remain in ramp-up and loss-making.
Management said the Q1 war situation partly disrupted the STP timeline; the start date may slip.
Confirmed order book conversion: the INR 4,000 crore pipeline depends on customer SOP timing (1-2 years).
ANM margins of about 6-8% weigh on the mix; the planned high-precision forging addition is at an early stage.
Two-wheeler exposure in India is in the low-margin ANM segment and faces competitive pressure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, the order book, and margin trajectory, with clear guidance for FY27. Less specific on the STP order book and on pass-through mechanics, and some answers on capacity and segment-level detail were loosely framed.
key_quotes: Overall, you can say that that in power train pollution about 70 75% businesses in global market.
So we focus more on providing the complete system rather than the components and we focus on the design to cause solutions for our customers.
And the important thing is that in the last 10 years, we have not lost any customer.

adds.what: New Bangalore EDU facility (EV transmission for electric bikes/scooters, customer River)
STP (Germany JV) forging and machining facility, about USD 10 million over 3-5 years
Hero Thailand project for BMW supply, new project expected from January 2027

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ (standalone Q2 up 27%, H1 consolidated up 23%), backed by a confirmed ~INR 4,000 crore lifetime order book with only INR 100-150 crore starting in FY27, plus the Bangalore EDU facility (live ~March-April 2027) and STP (calendar 2027), with the FY27 growth number itself not tied to a specific capacity figure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin up YoY in FY27 (H1 at 12.5%, +103 bps) and about 100 bps system-level uplift medium term, though subsidiaries are still loss-making and ANM margins sit at about 6-8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangalore EDU facility starts around March-April 2027 with INR 60-80 crore revenue in FY28; STP manufacturing starts calendar 2027, and Hero Thailand project starts January 2027, though STP timing may slip after the Q1 war disruption.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided 20%+ FY27 revenue growth; H1 standalone revenue is up 28% and consolidated up 23%, backed by a INR 4,000 crore lifetime order book with INR 100-150 crore starting in FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 70-75% across GNT, Bike Power Train and ANM, and management plans INR 200 crore of IPO-funded capex over two years plus about INR 150 crore maintenance capex, so further capex announcements are probable but not explicitly dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Standalone revenue grew 27% in Q2 and H1 consolidated grew 23%, against a 20%+ full-year guide, so there is room to lift the guide if the order book converts, but management has not signalled an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The STP start may slip after the Q1 war disruption, the INR 4,000 crore order book depends on 1-2 year SOP timing, and consolidated PAT margin is only 4.9% against standalone 7.3%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Formula racing transmission supply starts by end-calendar 2026, Bangalore EDU ramps over about one year, and marine design projects are starting at INR 5-20 crore each.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity down to 0.21x; interest cost falls to INR 1.5-2 crore per quarter
rows.why: INR 190 crore of loans repaid, with D/E falling from 0.89x at FY26 to 0.21x at H1 FY27, and quarterly interest expected to drop to INR 1.5-2 crore.

rows.label: Hero Thailand project supplying BMW Germany
rows.why: A new project is expected to start from Hero Thailand in January 2027, and overseas revenue is already 37-40% of the total.

rows.label: INR 100-150 crore of order book starting in FY27
rows.why: About INR 100-150 crore of the INR 4,000 crore confirmed lifetime order book starts in FY27, ramping to INR 500-600 crore a year by FY28-29.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20%+ FY27 growth, the confirmed order book and falling interest cost, but was less specific on the STP order book, pass-through mechanics and some capacity detail, which analysts pressed on.
